title: Voter Guide: 2026 Primary election - Maryland Matters

paragraphs.text: Election complete. See Maryland Matters's most recent political reporting here .

Maryland voters get their say this year on everything from county races to the governor’s office to the state’s eight representatives in Congress. But first, registered Democrats and Republicans will go to the polls on June 23 to select their nominees who will compete for those offices this fall.

Maryland Matters is offering a guide to all the races for state and federal office that will be on the primary ballot. We only included those races where there is more than one primary candidate for a seat. Check back with us after the dust has settled from the primary, when we’ll have a guide ready for the Nov. 3 general election.

Maryland Matters is deeply indebted to vote411.org , offered by the League of Women Voters Education Fund, for the answers to candidate questionnaires, and to our spring and summer interns, Rhiannon Evans , Will Hammann and Mayah Nachman , who did most of the heavy lifting here.

Material in this guide was taken from campaign websites, which was edited and condensed, and from candidate answers to the vote411.org survey, which were not edited. It’s a lot of info — if you find an error or omission, please let us know .

Democratic and Republican voters select their nominees June 23 for the local, state and federal races on the ballot Nov. 3. Maryland Matters is featuring only those state and federal races in our primary election guide where there is more than one candidate.

How do I register to vote?

You can register online or by mail until June 2. After that , you can go to an early voting center in your county during early in-person voting. Or on Election Day, go to the polling place assigned for your residence. In either case, you'll need a document that proves where you live, which can include your MVA-issued license, permit, ID card; a change of address card; your paycheck; a bank statement; a utility bill; another government document with your name and new address.
How do I get a mail-in ballot?
You have until June 16 to request a ballot by mail or fax. You can get an emailed link to get a ballot online until June 19.
I got a replacement ballot. What do I do now?

Because of an error in the printing and mailing of ballots, election officials have sent replacement ballots to anyone who was mailed a ballot before May 14. You will get a postcard or an email, or both, from the Maryland State Board of Elections to let you know if you'll get a replacement ballot, which are expected to be delivered by the first week of June. You should vote the replacement and destroy the original, but full directions are here .
How do I find a ballot drop box?
The list for all jurisdictions in the state is here .
Where can I go for early in-person voting?
Early voting centers are open June 11-18 from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., but may be different from your Election Day polling places. The list of early voting centers is here .
How do I find my polling place?
The Maryland State Board of Elections has a polling place finder site here .
How do I find my elected officials?
The Maryland State Board of Elections lets you find the races you care about by looking at a map or entering your address on its "Find my representatives" page.
